newsitem.title: USA: GE says global activity, Olympics helped revs.
newsitem.headline: GE says global activity, Olympics helped revs.

text.p: General Electric Co said Thursday that the increase in its third quarter revenues and operating margins reflect increased global activities and also revenues from the Summer Olympic games televised by its NBC television network.

In a release Thursday, GE said the increase in revenues for the third quarter of 1996 -- up 15 percent to $20 billion from $17.3 billion for the third quarter last year -- was a result of more global activity, revenues from the Summer Olympic games and higher sales of spare parts and services by the company's equipment businesses.
The company said that GE Capital Services' earnings increased 15 percent to $816 million, citing globalization and diversity of its 26 businesses.
GE Chairman John Welch said in the release that despite increasing global competition, the company "delivered another quarter of record results" from its global businesses.
"The businesses took significant steps to position the company for future growth," Welch said.

GE's NBC television network broadcast the Summer Olympic games to a U.S. audience of 209 million, the company said. It added that the network is expecting strong ratings for its new fall schedule, and NBC is positioning itself for the upcoming broadcasts of the 2000 through 2008 Olympics.

GE also said that Aircraft Engines won more than 60 percent of orders for large commercial engines in 1996, and that GE Capital Services expanded its auto leasing operations by acquiring Japan's Marubeni Car Systems.
GE Capital Services also acquired First Colony Corp, expanding into the insurance and annuity products market, the release noted.

GE added that cash generated from its operating activities through the first nine months of 1996 was $5.4 billion, up from last year's $2.4 billion, reflecting improvements in earnings and working capital.

As part of the $9 billion share repurchase plan, GE said it repurchased $674 million of its stock during the third quarter of 1996 to reach $5.6 billion, amounting to 85 million shares, purchased since December 1994.
